Factors to consider in feeding history.

Indicators of feeding and swallowing dysfunction/
aspiration.
• Facial weakness
• Decreased sensation
• Congestion, noisy “wet” sounds
• Multiple swallows to clear a bolus
• Unexplained fevers
• Unexplained irritability
• Coughing/choking/gagging before, during or after a swallow
• Food refusal
• Pain with swallowing
• Difﬁculty managing secretions, drooling
• History of upper respiratory infections, pneumonia
• Apnea during feeding
• Failure to thrive or maintain weight

There are numerous scales developed which assess feedings skills, oral intake, safe intake and nutritional status in children with
neurodevelopmental disabilities. Some are used for certain age groups, and others require special training to be able to administer.
Benfer et al. (2012) determined that the Schedule for Oral Motor Assessment (SOMA) and the Dysphagia Disorders Survey (DDS)
had the strongest clinical utility in pre-school children with neurodevelopmental disabilities. The EDACS mentioned earlier, is
